name: content-modeling trigger queries
description: Should trigger when the author-facing structure of a block (table layout, what authors type) must be designed or reviewed; near misses are code, import, tests, UE models and finding existing blocks.

queries.query: Marketing wants a testimonial block: quote, person's name and role, headshot, and several of them side by side. Before any code, decide what the authors will type in their documents and give me the table layout.
In the cards block, product wants some cards marked "featured" so they render bigger. How should authors mark a card as featured? Just the authoring side for now, I'll do the CSS.

A dev proposed this model for our new pricing block. Review it from an author's point of view:

| pricing |
| tier | Pro |
| price | 29 |
| period | month |
| feature1 | 10 users |
| feature2 | priority support |
| cta-text | Start trial |
| cta-link | /signup |
We want a tabs component where each tab holds a grid of cards. How should authors build this in Word or Google Docs so it stays easy for them?
The site needs a contact form with name, email and message, plus a newsletter signup form on the footer. What do authors put in the document to get these forms?

Design handed over an intro section: a small label, an H2, two paragraphs and a centered button. A colleague wants a `text-intro` block for it so styling is consistent. Is that the right call, and what should authors do?
Our `stats` block has authors fill in a table with 7 columns (icon, number, unit, label, caption, link, style) per row and they keep getting it wrong. Redesign the structure so it's easy for authors.
We need a feature comparison for 8 features across 5 plans, mostly ticks and short values, shown on the pricing page. How do authors provide that data and what block structure do we use?
Add a block for our team's recommended reading list: book cover, title, author, one-line reason and a link to buy. I haven't thought about how authors will enter it.
We're adding a `promo-banner` block (image, headline, short text, one button) and our authors work in Universal Editor. Design the block so it's easy for them to use, then build it.
The cards block looks broken on tablet: the third card wraps under the first two and the images stretch. Fix the CSS.
The model is decided: each row of the `quote` block has two cells, an image in the first and a blockquote plus attribution in the second. Write quote.js and quote.css for it.
Take https://www.example-bakery.com/about and bring that page into our EDS project as authored content, reusing our existing blocks.
Is there an accordion block in Adobe's Block Collection I can start from? Show me where it lives and how it's used.
Add the cards block to our Universal Editor setup: I need the component definition, a model with image and text fields, and the filters.
Please review PR #214 on our EDS repo. Someone added a tabs block; check the JS and CSS for bugs and accessibility problems.
`aem up` dies immediately with EADDRINUSE and I don't know what is on the port. How do I fix it?
Write Playwright tests for the hero block that check the heading and the CTA link render and that the image has an alt attribute.
Lighthouse says our LCP is 4s on mobile, mostly because the hero image loads late. What should I change in the project's scripts and the hero block?
